crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Satellite Imagery
children.blurb: Satellite imagery as alternative data refers to the use of overhead optical, radar, and multispectral images to measure economic activity that is not captured in standard financial statements or government releases.

children.name: Card Transaction Data
children.blurb: Card transaction data refers to aggregated and anonymized records of purchases made with credit, debit, and prepaid cards, used by economists and analysts to track consumer spending, revenue trends, and regional economic activity.

children.name: Sensor and Shipping Data
children.blurb: Sensor and shipping data as alternative data covers physical-world signals from vessel transponders, port sensors, weather stations and cargo telemetry, used to estimate trade flows, commodity supply, congestion and industrial activity.

children.name: Mobile Location Data
children.blurb: Mobile location data refers to aggregated or individual-level geospatial records collected from smartphones and other connected devices, used as an alternative dataset for economic analysis, retail footfall, mobility, and real estate.

children.name: Web Data Collection
children.blurb: Web data collection in alternative data means gathering publicly available information from websites, forums, job boards, app stores, social media, and regulatory filings to build datasets that supplement traditional financial and economic data.

sections.body: Alternative data refers to information gathered outside standard financial statements and market prices, used to estimate economic activity. In practice, artificial intelligence processes satellite photos to count cars in retail parking lots or measure crop health, reads anonymized card transaction records to track spending by category, and parses shipping transponder signals to estimate port congestion. It also works with mobile location pings to measure foot traffic at stores or factories and scrapes public web pages for job postings, prices, and product availability. These systems turn raw feeds into time series and indicators that economists and trading desks compare against official statistics. The work is operational now, not experimental, with vendors selling feeds and models that update daily or intraday. The AI part is mostly computer vision, natural language processing, and time series forecasting applied to very large, messy datasets.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field has solved basic ingestion and cleaning for many common sources, such as aligning satellite tiles and matching card transactions to merchant categories. What remains hard is consistency across time and geography, because sensor coverage, privacy rules, and vendor methods change without notice. Honest limits include noisy signals, survivorship bias in web data, and the fact that alternative data often correlates with official data but does not replace it. Models can overfit to a short history, and backtests frequently look better than live performance. There is no single standard for accuracy, and many feeds are sold with little independent audit. The result is useful but uneven, with strong results in narrow tasks like counting ships or cars and weaker results in broad economic nowcasting.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The Satellite Imagery page explains how models read overhead photos for physical activity, from oil storage shadows to construction progress. Card Transaction Data covers spending panels and the AI used to normalize merchant names and detect anomalies in consumer behavior. Sensor and Shipping Data describes vessel transponders, truck GPS, and industrial sensors, and how their signals become supply chain indicators. Mobile Location Data walks through foot traffic measurement and the privacy and sampling issues that shape its reliability. Web Data Collection covers scraping, parsing, and deduplication of public pages for prices, listings, and text. Together they move from physical observation to financial transaction to movement to human mobility to open text, and a reader can follow that order to see how each source fills a different gap in official statistics.
